Bococizumab and LDL cholesterol: the measure was corrected in 2026, and the evidence base was checked for the first time in 2026-08

In adults with primary hyperlipidaemia, mixed dyslipidaemia or heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia, what is the effect of bococizumab compared with placebo or an active lipid-lowering comparator on the percent change from baseline in LDL cholesterol at week 12?

Eligibility criteriaPopulation: adults with a lipid disorder -- primary hyperlipidaemia, mixed dyslipidaemia, hypercholesterolaemia, or heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia. A record whose only condition is `Healthy` is not in this population, and that limb removes the phase-1 pharmacology programme; a record whose only condition is `Cardiovascular Disease` is the SPIRE-1/SPIRE-2 outcomes programme, which asks a different question with a different endpoint. Intervention: bococizumab as the randomised intervention, matched against the declared synonym set including the development codes PF-04950615 and RN316 -- eleven of the twenty-two registrations name the drug by a code. Comparator: placebo or an active lipid-lowering comparator, read from arm type **or** from what the arms receive, because each reading is blind to a real design the other sees. Estimand, which governs poolability and not eligibility: percent change from baseline in LDL-C at week 12, detected structurally at every rank rather than by the registered phrase. The timepoint is part of the estimand. Criteria are derived post hoc and say so.

What was measured

Table 9. What was measured
Comparatorplacebo
Estimandpercent change from baseline — random-effects
Effect scalereported on the log scale; nothing is pooled on this outcome

Pooled result

Estimate withdrawn. The endpoints agree and the measure is the defect -- which makes this the opposite of every other topic in this PASS. All three registrations read declare the same primary, verbatim: 'Percent Change From Baseline in Fasting Low Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol (LDL-C) at Week 12'. That is a continuous quantity. It has no events. An odds ratio requires a 2x2 table of participants who did and did not experience something, and a percent change in a laboratory value produces no such table. This page derived one anyway. What the counts actually are is not recorded, and their magnitude shows they are not events: spire-ldl is stored as 971 in 1,068 placebo participants -- 91 per cent -- which is a threshold or responder flag of some kind, applied to an endpoint whose registered form is a mean change. Deriving an odds ratio from an undocumented dichotomisation of a continuous outcome discards the effect size the trials were designed to estimate and replaces it with a quantity that depends entirely on where the unrecorded threshold was placed.

What this does not establish: not that bococizumab does not lower LDL cholesterol -- it does, substantially, and these trials were designed to measure by how much. The trials here measure a mean percent change in LDL-C, a continuous quantity, and nothing on this page estimates the question its title implies. What is confirmed: the original withdrawal was right and its one-line reason -- 'odds ratio on a continuous LDL-C endpoint' -- is precisely correct, which re-verification establishes rather than assumes. All trial identities are correct and all three registered primaries are the same endpoint. The replacement question is available and parked: these trials share an estimand exactly, so a mean difference synthesis is genuinely defensible -- it needs each trial's least-squares mean difference read from its results record, which is a source-document step this pass did not take.

Percent change from baseline in LDL-C at week 12 -- a continuous outcome. k = 3.

What was measured

Table 12. What was measured
Comparatorplacebo
Estimandmean percent change from baseline — random-effects

Pooled result

MD -55.24 (-57.92 to -52.56), 95% interval

Percent change from baseline in fasting LDL-C at week 12. random-effects, estimator REML random-effects, inverse-variance, k = 6.

τ² 5.842 · I² 56.8% · Q 11.59 on 5 df

Favours: the intervention (lower is better)

I-squared 56.8 per cent and tau-squared 5.84 under REML, over k=6. Both fell when the sixth trial joined -- I-squared from 65.1 and tau-squared from 9.31 -- and that is not evidence that the pool became more coherent. Coherence was established by reading six endpoint definitions and would be identical at any I-squared (P36).

Six trials register the identical primary -- percent change from baseline in LDL-C at week 12 -- and every value pooled is the trial's own least-squares mean difference, read from its posted `analyses` block. Not one is derived by us. The estimand was never the problem on this topic; the measure was, and the measure was corrected in 2026-08. What was still missing was any evidence that these were the right six trials, and the executed search of 2026-08-19 supplied it: SPIRE-FH (NCT01968980, n=370) was surfaced by this review's own query, passed its own criteria, and was absent from the object. Four more are eligible, have posted LDL results, and still cannot contribute, because each randomised dose rather than drug-against-placebo -- inside NCT01342211 alone the effect runs from -2.30 to -49.11 percentage points, a spread wider than this entire pool. Eligible with results is not poolable.

A confirmation is a result, not a null.

Table 13. A confirmation is a result, not a null.
knestimateI²
before the check54079-55.46 (-58.84 to -52.07)65.1%
after64449-55.24 (-57.92 to -52.56)56.8%

The pooled mean difference by 0.22 percentage points; k by one trial and 370 participants; tau-squared from 9.31 to 5.84.

Before the search, nobody could tell 'right' from 'unexamined and lucky', and from the outside the two are identical. This review's five trials were the five somebody once put on a page. That they turned out to be very nearly the right five is a fact that only exists because the check was run -- it was not available beforehand and could not have been inferred from the page, the estimate, or the care taken over the measure. The check is what distinguishes a correct estimate from a lucky one, and it is worth exactly as much when it confirms.

On one night, on one corpus, the same discipline moved a poolable set UP (apixaban prophylaxis, 3 -> 8), down (apixaban treatment, 8 -> 3), and not at all (here). A procedure that only ever produced convenient answers would be indistinguishable from no procedure. These three together are what make it a check, and none of the three was arranged.

SPIRE-AI registers four arms in a dose-matched double-dummy -- bococizumab 150 mg, bococizumab 75 mg, and a matching placebo for each. This pool's spire-ai row pairs the 150 mg dose with the 75 mg placebo. Both are real registered arms and together they are not a registered contrast. Established from the registry's arm table; not corrected, because the stored value derives from these arms.

Six of SPIRE-AI's seven registered primary outcomes concern the percentage of injections meeting a successful-assessment definition on a participant assessment tool -- it is an auto-injector usability trial. The seventh is the LDL-C change pooled here. The selection is recorded nowhere.

SPIRE-SI registers bococizumab, atorvastatin and placebo. This object records two arms and does not record which was dropped.

The methods rule governing this decision

Decision: Cochrane Handbook 6.5.1 s10.10.4.4: REML is preferred to DerSimonian-Laird for the between-study variance, and is the RevMan default.

Does the answer depend on the pooling method?

This is a new analysis, so the estimator was chosen correctly from the start rather than inherited: REML, per the house rule below k=10.

Table 18. Does the answer depend on the pooling method?
Between-study varianceIntervalSummary (95% CI)τ²
restricted maximum likelihood (REML)ordinary (Wald)-55.46 (-58.84 to -52.07)9.315
restricted maximum likelihood (REML)Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman (HKSJ)-55.46 (-60.67 to -50.25)9.315
DerSimonian-Laird (DL)ordinary (Wald)-55.43 (-58.65 to -52.21)8.039
DerSimonian-Laird (DL)Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman (HKSJ)-55.43 (-60.58 to -50.28)8.039
Paule-Mandel (PM)ordinary (Wald)-55.53 (-59.3 to -51.76)12.66
Paule-Mandel (PM)Hartung-Knapp-Sidik-Jonkman (HKSJ)-55.53 (-60.88 to -50.19)12.66

The point spans -55.43 to -55.53 across all six combinations -- three hundredths of a percentage point. The interval is what the method changes: Wald about -59 to -52, Hartung-Knapp about -61 to -50, and at k=5 with I-squared 65 per cent hartung-knapp is the honest one. Every combination excludes no effect by an enormous margin.

REML with a Wald interval is the headline, with Hartung-Knapp shown beside it. Nothing here was inherited from the withdrawn analysis.

Risk of bias, both assessors

⬇ SVG (vector) 22 KB

Only the vector format is offered for this figure, by choice: it is line art — discrete marks, glyphs and labels — which SVG reproduces exactly at any size, so a raster would add weight without adding fidelity. The build was able to rasterise; it was asked not to.

Every cell carries BOTH independent cross-family assessments and they are not reconciled: showing one column would be a reconciliation presented as an observation. Glyph as well as colour, so the panel survives greyscale printing and colour-blind reading. A trial with no judgement is shown as a row of not-assessed markers rather than omitted, so a gap in the assessment cannot be mistaken for a clean assessment. Agreement as measured: {'per domain agreed': 24, 'per domain total': 30, 'per domain rate pct': 80.0, 'recomputed from the stored judgements': True, 'why recomputed': 'The stored disagreement tallies were frozen as text and 12 of 22 no longer match the judgements in the object -- a later guidance pass moved 51 the randomisation process judgements and the tallies were never recomputed. This is derived from what the object holds now.'}.

Other recorded qualifications

Statements this review records about the limits of what it establishes, which are not shown elsewhere on this page. They are reproduced from the object verbatim and are not summarised.

Table 21. Other recorded qualifications
And a dose ranging design is eligible and not poolableStated here rather than discovered at the pooling step. A dose-ranging trial randomised dose; pooling one of its arms against placebo means choosing which arm, and no rule in this review chooses it. Inside NCT01342211 alone the effect runs from -2.30 to -49.11 percentage points -- a spread wider than the entire pool. The choice would be ours and it would look like the trial's.
Components as the registry states themPercent change from baseline in fasting ldl-c at week 12. A continuous quantity. There are no events to count.
Analysis set as the registry states itWeek 12. Note: the counts stored here imply 971 'events' in 1,068 placebo participants -- 91 per cent -- which is not an event rate but a threshold or responder flag, applied to an endpoint that has no events.
Components as the registry states thempercent change in LDL-C from baseline to week 12. One continuous quantity, one anchor, one time point.
Components as the registry states themPercent change from baseline in fasting ldl-c at week 12. Continuous.
Components as the registry states themPercent change from baseline in ldl-c at week 12. Continuous.
Why that is a finding and not a null resultBefore the search, nobody could tell 'right' from 'unexamined and lucky', and from the outside the two are identical. This review's five trials were the five somebody once put on a page. That they turned out to be very nearly the right five is a fact that only exists because the check was run -- it was not available beforehand and could not have been inferred from the page, the estimate, or the care taken over the measure. The check is what distinguishes a correct estimate from a lucky one, and it is worth exactly as much when it confirms.
And the reverse reading is available tooA reader may take this as evidence the original page was competently built, and that reading is supported: the estimate was right, the measure was corrected properly, and the five trials were nearly the whole of the evidence. Both readings are compatible, and only one of them was checkable before 2026-08-19.
The se construction is stated not hiddenNo source printed a standard error for any of the six results, so every SE is derived from the published interval: se = (hi - lo) / (2 * qnorm(0.975)). The refit inherits that construction and the script prints each derived SE beside its interval so a reader can check the derivation rather than take it.
Why absentk=6 and a pool was computed -- it is on this page -- but not by a model call this object can quote. There is no R session, no printed output and no package version, so P6 refuses on the quotation and not on the synthesis. The arithmetic is reproducible from the script named on the outcome; a quotable metafor call is what is missing and what would hold P6.
The refit reproduces the stored fit exactlyStored: MD -55.24 (-57.92 to -52.56), I-squared 56.8, tau-squared 5.8423, Q 11.5854 on df 5. Refit under metafor REML: -55.2406 (-57.9243 to -52.5569), I-squared 56.66, tau-squared 5.8423, Q 11.5854 on df 5. The point, the interval, the heterogeneity and the q statistic all reproduce.
A correction to a claim made earlier tonightThe first version of ssot/boco_refit.R printed a check line asserting the stored values were 'MD -55.24 (-58.27 to -52.21), I^2 = 41.5' and reported that the heterogeneity did not reproduce. Those stored values were never read from the object -- they were typed into the script from nothing, and 41.5 is the stored I-squared of a different topic, sglt2-ckd-review. The object has always held 56.8. There was no discrepancy and i reported one. Corrected here rather than quietly removed, because the corpus-wide sweep run immediately afterwards listed five divergent pools and bococizumab was not among them -- the sweep contradicted the claim at the moment it was made and the contradiction went unread.
A spire ai pairs a dose with the other doses placeboSPIRE-AI registers four arms in a dose-matched double-dummy -- bococizumab 150 mg, bococizumab 75 mg, and a matching placebo for each. This pool's spire-ai row pairs the 150 mg dose with the 75 mg placebo. Both are real registered arms and together they are not a registered contrast. Established from the registry's arm table; not corrected, because the stored value derives from these arms.
B spire ai registers seven primaries and one is pooledSix of SPIRE-AI's seven registered primary outcomes concern the percentage of injections meeting a successful-assessment definition on a participant assessment tool -- it is an auto-injector usability trial. The seventh is the LDL-C change pooled here. The selection is recorded nowhere.
C spire si registers three arms one of them atorvastatinSPIRE-SI registers bococizumab, atorvastatin and placebo. This object records two arms and does not record which was dropped.
And no query missed an included trial hereSaid plainly, because three other topics in this corpus lost one to theirs. sglt2-hf lost DELIVER and iv-iron-hf lost AFFIRM-AHF and HEART-FID to condition terms one word too narrow; apixaban-vte lost NCT02366871 to a phase filter. A clean recall is only worth reading if the misses are reported in the same voice, so it is reported here in that voice.
And four more are eligible with results and do not poolNCT01342211, NCT01350141, NCT02055976 and NCT01592240. Each randomised dose. Eligible with results is not poolable, and the four are named on the page with their own numbers so the refusal costs something inspectable.
What eligible poolable not included meansA gap in our own evidence base, not the literature's. Each was surfaced by this review's own search, passed its own criteria, has posted LDL results, and was not in the object -- because this review had no executed search until 2026-08-19.
And the shape of the remainder is the diagnosisSeven of 22 fail a criterion and four of the five recovered trials are eligible with results and still cannot contribute. That is neither a query that is too broad nor a field still in flight: it is a development programme whose early phase is dose-ranging by design. No better query recovers a single contrast from a trial that randomised four doses.
Why this is not an adjudicated disputeA blind second assessor from a different model family disagreed with this domain on 89% of judgements across 22 topics. That would ordinarily be a dispute to adjudicate. It is not one: the tool's own text names this exact evidential situation -- a bare statement that a study was randomised -- and prescribes the answer. The second assessor is not being deferred ; the guidance is being applied.
What the registry gives and does notA ClinicalTrials.gov design module records `allocation: Randomized`. It carries no sequence-generation method and no allocation-concealment mechanism. The original judgement's own note said so before scoring LOW.
How this maps to the tool s algorithmThe tool maps 'No information' on 1.1 and 1.2 with no baseline concern to a domain judgement of some concerns. This project writes no information on the domain when it could not be judged from the sources read, and caps the overall at some concerns. Same place, and it keeps 'we could not judge this' distinguishable from 'we judged it and had concerns'.
What does not changeNo overall rating and no GRADE CERTAINTY moves. All 51 judgements were already capped at some concerns or HIGH by another no information domain.
This does not replace the stored judgementThis is the judgement the published algorithm proposes from the signalling responses named here. It does not replace the stored `judgement` beside it, and nothing reads it yet. The tool itself says its algorithms "provide proposed judgements, but users should verify these and change them if they feel this is appropriate" -- so this is an input to a person, not an output to a reader.
Identity established from the registry arm tableSPIRE-AI registers four arms in a dose-matched double-dummy: Bococizumab 150mg, Bococizumab 75mg, Bococizumab 150mg placebo, Bococizumab 75mg placebo. This object pairs 'Bococizumab 150mg' with 'Bococizumab 75mg placebo' -- both real registered arms, and not a registered contrast, because the 150 mg dose's comparator is the 150 mg placebo. Established from the registry's own arm table before any domain was judged, and not corrected: the stored MD -63.4 derives from these arms, so a correction moves a published number.
And it bounds a finding of oursClass 94 records assessor 2 saying no information on the randomisation process/deviations from the intended intervention/missing outcome data `100 of 100`. Measured across all 23 topics now stored that is 239 of 243, and all four exceptions are the randomisation process=some concerns on `agyw-hiv-prep-review` and `cab-prep-hiv-review` -- two of the three topics asked under the earlier prompt build, the one whose reply ids are bare NCTs. Under that build it is 4 of 6; under the later build 0 of 75. The 100% was measured on the later build's topics. The two-defaults mechanism stands; its universality does not, and what varies with it is the prompt.
The rate is still conditional on the same allow listBoth numbers are conditional on the fact list in THE_ALLOW_LIST_THE_RATE_IS_CONDITIONAL_ON above. Neither is a rate of agreement between assessors in general.
What this review does not publishWhat this review does not publish. This review also examined one outcome for which no pooled estimate is published: Percent change from baseline in LDL-C at week 12 -- a continuous outcome (k=3) -- the endpoints agree and the measure is the defect -- which makes this the opposite of ever. Each of those outcomes is recorded on this review with the reason it was not pooled, and none of them contributes to the estimate reported above (-55.24 at k=6). A reader meeting the pooled result should not take it as covering every outcome, or every trial, this review examined. This sentence exists because a second, independent reading -- by a different model family, given the object and the abstract and none of our conclusions -- found that a reader would reasonably conclude the review pools all relevant trials, and that the object does not support that. The withdrawals were already recorded beside the outcomes they concern; they were invisible from the abstract, which is where the impression forms.
Which risk of bias domains drove the ratingWhere a result is rated worse than LOW overall, the domain carrying that judgement is: selection of the reported result on 2 result(s). The overall rating is the worst domain, so these are the domains that determine it.

Paper

Each statement below cites the record it came from; those sources are listed at the end of every section. Where the record holds nothing, the section says so by name rather than being left out, so a procedure that was not carried out can be told from one that simply was never mentioned.

Title

Bococizumab and LDL cholesterol: the measure was corrected in 2026, and the evidence base was checked for the first time in 2026-081

Sources for this section (1)
  1. title

Abstract

Question. In adults with primary hyperlipidaemia, mixed dyslipidaemia or heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia, what is the effect of bococizumab compared with placebo or an active lipid-lowering comparator on the percent change from baseline in LDL cholesterol at week 12?1

Methods. ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 and PubMed (ncbi e-utilities esearch) were searched; estimates were pooled under a random-effects model with the REML random-effects, inverse-variance estimator; risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials); and certainty was rated with GRADE.2

Results. Percent change from baseline in fasting LDL-C at week 12: mean difference -55.2 (-57.9 to -52.6) across 6 trials; 1 of these pooled outcome(s) carries a stated qualification -- a referral or a recorded finding -- given in full in Results and not reproduced here; the trials agreed moderately (I-squared 56.8%); and certainty of the evidence was low.3

Introduction

Background. This review asks: In adults with primary hyperlipidaemia, mixed dyslipidaemia or heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia, what is the effect of bococizumab compared with placebo or an active lipid-lowering comparator on the percent change from baseline in LDL cholesterol at week 12? It pools 6 randomised trials comprising 4,449 participants as registered, against placebo. The outcomes pooled are Percent change from baseline in LDL-C at week 12 -- a continuous outcome; Percent change from baseline in fasting LDL-C at week 12.1

Sources for this section (1)
  1. manuscript.introduction

Methods — search

Searches were executed in ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 on 2026-08-19 with the query, verbatim: intervention="bococizumab"; study_type=interventional; no phase filter; page_size=100; count_total=true. It returned 22 record(s).1

Searches were executed in ClinicalTrials.gov API v2 -- second query, recorded because it differs on 2026-08-19 with the query, verbatim: condition="hypercholesterolemia OR dyslipidemia OR cardiovascular disease"; intervention="bococizumab"; study_type=interventional. It returned 21 record(s).2

Searches were executed in PubMed (ncbi e-utilities esearch) on 2026-08-19 with the query, verbatim: bococizumab. It returned 50 record(s).3

Methods — eligibility criteria

Population: adults with a lipid disorder -- primary hyperlipidaemia, mixed dyslipidaemia, hypercholesterolaemia, or heterozygous familial hypercholesterolaemia. A record whose only condition is `Healthy` is not in this population, and that limb removes the phase-1 pharmacology programme; a record whose only condition is `Cardiovascular Disease` is the SPIRE-1/SPIRE-2 outcomes programme, which asks a different question with a different endpoint. Intervention: bococizumab as the randomised intervention, matched against the declared synonym set including the development codes PF-04950615 and RN316 -- eleven of the twenty-two registrations name the drug by a code. Comparator: placebo or an active lipid-lowering comparator, read from arm type **or** from what the arms receive, because each reading is blind to a real design the other sees. Estimand, which governs poolability and not eligibility: percent change from baseline in LDL-C at week 12, detected structurally at every rank rather than by the registered phrase. The timepoint is part of the estimand. Criteria are derived post hoc and say so.1

Each criterion above is recorded with the source it was derived from in `screening.eligibility_provenance`; none is asserted here without one.2

Methods — outcomes sought at every registered rank

Before deciding which outcomes could be combined, every trial was read at every registered rank -- primary, secondary and other -- asking: does each eligible trial register a percent change in ldl-c outcome at any rank -- primary, secondary or other -- before concluding which trials can be combined? Asked at every registered rank before concluding which trials can be combined, and detected structurally -- an LDL term plus a change term -- rather than by the registered phrase. Matching the five incumbents' wording would have found the five that already agree and nothing else, which is the method that made eight apixaban trials look poolable when three were. Yes for ten of the twenty-two, and that did not settle poolability: six pool, and four are eligible with posted results and cannot contribute a single contrast because each randomised dose.1

Sources for this section (1)

Methods — synthesis

For percent change from baseline in fasting LDL-C at week 12, a random-effects model was fitted with the REML random-effects, inverse-variance estimator.1

Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 (Cochrane risk-of-bias tool for randomized trials) , following . 6 result-level assessments were made.2

A ceiling applies to every risk-of-bias judgement in this review; it is stated with the assessment itself rather than summarised here.3

Certainty of evidence was rated with GRADE, following Cochrane Handbook for Systematic Reviews of Interventions version 6.5.1, Chapter 14. HIGH for a body of randomised evidence, then rated down. 1 pooled outcome(s) were rated. No domain is rated up.4

Results

The pooled mean difference for percent change from baseline in fasting LDL-C at week 12 was -55.2 (-57.9 to -52.6) across 6 trials, against placebo.1

Noted on this pool. SPIRE-AI registers four arms in a dose-matched double-dummy -- bococizumab 150 mg, bococizumab 75 mg, and a matching placebo for each. This pool's spire-ai row pairs the 150 mg dose with the 75 mg placebo. Both are real registered arms and together they are not a registered contrast. Established from the registry's arm table; not corrected, because the stored value derives from these arms. Six of SPIRE-AI's seven registered primary outcomes concern the percentage of injections meeting a successful-assessment definition on a participant assessment tool -- it is an auto-injector usability trial. The seventh is the LDL-C change pooled here. The selection is recorded nowhere. SPIRE-SI registers bococizumab, atorvastatin and placebo. This object records two arms and does not record which was dropped.2

The trials' results were moderately consistent with one another: I-squared, the share of the variation between them that is more than chance alone would produce, was 56.8%; the estimated variance of the true effects between trials (tau-squared) was 5.84, the heterogeneity test statistic Q was 11.6, on degrees of freedom 5. I-squared 56.8 per cent and tau-squared 5.84 under REML, over k=6. Both fell when the sixth trial joined -- I-squared from 65.1 and tau-squared from 9.31 -- and that is not evidence that the pool became more coherent. Coherence was established by reading six endpoint definitions and would be identical at any I-squared (P36).3

The grounds for pooling are recorded as: Six trials register the identical primary -- percent change from baseline in LDL-C at week 12 -- and every value pooled is the trial's own least-squares mean difference, read from its posted `analyses` block. Not one is derived by us. The estimand was never the problem on this topic; the measure was, and the measure was corrected in 2026-08. What was still missing was any evidence that these were the right six trials, and the executed search of 2026-08-19 supplied it: SPIRE-FH (NCT01968980, n=370) was surfaced by this review's own query, passed its own criteria, and was absent from the object. Four more are eligible, have posted LDL results, and still cannot contribute, because each randomised dose rather than drug-against-placebo -- inside NCT01342211 alone the effect runs from -2.30 to -49.11 percentage points, a spread wider than this entire pool. Eligible with results is not poolable. Where a later pool on this page rests on the same grounds, they are not restated.4

Percent change from baseline in LDL-C at week 12 -- a continuous outcome. These 3 trials are not pooled, and the reason is stated rather than the outcome being quietly omitted: The endpoints agree and the measure is the defect -- which makes this the opposite of every other topic in this pass. All three registrations read declare the same primary, verbatim: 'Percent Change From Baseline in Fasting Low Density Lipoprotein Cholesterol (LDL-C) at Week 12'. That is a continuous quantity. It has no events. An odds ratio requires a 2x2 table of participants who did and did not experience something, and a percent change in a laboratory value produces no such table. This page derived one anyway. What the counts actually are is not recorded, and their magnitude shows they are not events: spire-ldl is stored as 971 in 1,068 placebo participants -- 91 per cent -- which is a threshold or responder flag of some kind, applied to an endpoint whose registered form is a mean change. Deriving an odds ratio from an undocumented dichotomisation of a continuous outcome discards the effect size the trials were designed to estimate and replaces it with a quantity that depends entirely on where the unrecorded threshold was placed.5

The full model output for every pooled outcome -- the call, the estimator, the heterogeneity statistics and the back-transformed interval -- is reproduced verbatim as Extended data at the end of this article, so every number above can be checked against the software that produced it.6

Risk of bias in the included results

Risk of bias was assessed with RoB 2 at the level of each reported result. Across the 6 results assessed: 6 at some concerns. The per-domain judgements behind them are recorded with the extracted data.1

Certainty of the evidence

Certainty was rated with GRADE. HIGH for a body of randomised evidence, then rated down.1

No domain is rated up.2

Where a result is rated worse than LOW overall, the domain carrying that judgement is: selection of the reported result on 2 result(s). The overall rating is the worst domain, so these are the domains that determine it.3

Certainty of the evidence, by outcome, with every rating step4
OutcomeCertaintykStarted atRating steps
percent change from baseline in fasting LDL-C at week 12LOW6HIGHrisk of bias: HIGH to MODERATE, down 1 level(s) -- No result-level RoB 2 assessment exists for this outcome. Rated down one level because unassessed is not low.; inconsistency: MODERATE to LOW, down 1 level(s) -- I-squared 56.8 per cent over k=6, with per-trial mean differences from -49.9 to -63.4 percentage points. Rated down for the spread. This is inconsistency of result and says nothing about whether the estimand is shared, which was established by reading six registered titles.; indirectness: not rated down -- One comparator class, one endpoint, one timepoint, verified by reading each trial's registered text. The outcome is a surrogate -- LDL cholesterol, not a clinical event -- and that is stated rather than rated down here, because the review's question names the surrogate explicitly. A reader who wants clinical outcomes is asking a different question, and bococizumab's two outcome trials, SPIRE-1 and SPIRE-2, were terminated.; imprecision: not rated down -- k=6, 4,449 participants, interval -57.9 to -52.6 percentage points. The interval excludes no effect by a wide margin and is narrow relative to the effect. Not rated down.; publication bias: not rated down -- k=6. A funnel plot at k=6 has little power and would be theatre. Not assessed, and not counted as absent. One relevant fact IS recorded: the entire programme is one sponsor's, and it was discontinued -- the direction that hazard runs is unknown.

Limitations

Eligible trials that do not contribute: All included registrations carry a row in this object.1

This review does not claim that any per-trial count was checked against a results record.2

What this review does not give a clinician: the number of events in each arm, any absolute effect or number needed to treat and any measure of harm. A relative effect cannot be turned into the benefit or the risk facing one patient without them, so this review can support a judgement about what these trials found and not a judgement about what to do.3

The withholding question, asked at every rank

does each eligible trial register a PERCENT CHANGE IN LDL-C outcome at ANY rank -- primary, secondary or other -- before concluding which trials can be combined?

YES FOR TEN OF THE TWENTY-TWO, AND THAT DID NOT SETTLE POOLABILITY: six pool, and four are eligible with posted results and cannot contribute a single contrast because each randomised DOSE.

Asked at EVERY registered rank before concluding which trials can be combined, and detected STRUCTURALLY -- an LDL term plus a change term -- rather than by the registered phrase. Matching the five incumbents' wording would have found the five that already agree and nothing else, which is the method that made eight apixaban trials look poolable when three were.

Published-meta comparison — PENDING_EXTERNAL_RESOLUTION

Denominator: —. Not yet established. Establishing it requires resolving published syntheses' included-sets to REGISTRATION IDs. A second lane has validated that pipeline (stated-k table identification plus two-hop citation->PMID->registration) and is running it now.

Explicitly not done: CITATION-STRING MATCHING. It would produce a comparison-shaped answer tonight and it is not identity: two syntheses citing the same trial under different labels would read as different, and the same label on different trials as the same. That is the substitution class this project audits for.

Blocked on: lane 2 registration-id resolution
